findings: l.1124: the condition 2g - 2 + s > 0 is exactly the non-metabelian range of the marked surface group of l.1140: for 2g-2+s>0 it surjects onto the free group F2 (g>=2: a1,b1,a2,b2 -> x,y,y,x; g>=1,s>=1: a1,b1,c1 -> x,y,[x,y]^-1; g=0,s>=3: c1,c2,c3 -> x,y,(xy)^-1; every other generator -> 1), and for 2g-2+s<=0 ((g,s) in {(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,0)}) it is abelian. Proved both ways (SurfaceGroup.isMetabelianGroup_iff). No defect in the paper here.
questions: l.1148 'anabelian fundamental group': read as 'not metabelian', the hypothesis of the strict GX.e0RegM_holonomy (as Admissible.lean already does). Under 2g-2+s>0 the marked group maps onto F2, so it is non-abelian, non-metabelian and non-solvable, and each of the usual readings (non-abelian, non-metabelian, non-solvable) is implied by the algebra; the reading only matters for which hypothesis Barbot's input consumes.

kb_proposals: To refute metabelianity of a presented group, surject onto FreeGroup (Fin 2) via PresentedGroup.toGroup and use the strict GX.freeGroup_not_isMetabelianGroup; no finite group (S4) and no decide is needed. Surjectivity: MonoidHom.range_eq_top + FreeGroup.closure_range_of + Subgroup.closure_le, then fin_cases.

Relator checks under PresentedGroup.toGroup: rewrite FreeGroup.lift of the relator into List.ofFn products, simp [List.ofFn_succ, the generator map, Fin.succ_ne_zero, i.succ.succ != 1 lemmas], then simp only [commutatorElement_def]; group. Avoid Fin.ext_iff in that simp (it loops on the if-chain definitions).
